answer: An agent network monitoring a coastal lagoon can mitigate Sybil attacks using memory-hard proof-of-work. Before verifying telemetry across a shale basin or access bridge, each agent must resolve sequential memory lookups to solve a cryptographic puzzle. An attacker incurs the verifiable expenditure of scarce memory bandwidth and electrical power per identity. However, this mechanism penalizes low-power edge sensors while failing against adversaries with dedicated parallel compute.
